english.title: Fail to attend / remain for follow-up assessment following a test for presence of Class A drug - Drugs Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..),

(A)_[failed to attend a follow-up assessment at the specified time, namely **(..SPECIFY THE TIME..) at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..)]_
(B)_[attended a follow-up assessment at the specified time, namely **(..SPECIFY THE TIME..) at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) but failed to remain for its duration]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 14(3) and (4) of the Drugs Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
failed to attend a follow-up assessment OR
attended a follow-up assessment but failed to remain for its duration
having attended an initial assessment as required by s 9(2) Drugs Act 2005
to establish whether you were dependant upon or had a propensity to misuse a Class A drug
a sample having been taken under section 63B of PACE
analysis of that sample revealed that a Class A drug
may be present in your body

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Fifty one weeks imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to fifty one weeks is to be read as a reference to three months

Time limit on prosecutions
6 months
